page: Microsoft Azure FX96mds_v2 is a high-memory compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Its cache subsystem features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Memory capacity totals 1,832 GB, delivering approximately 19.08 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided through a bundled 5,669 GB NVMe solid-state drive.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high throughput across memory and compute subsystems. Multi-core performance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 103,610.4 and a stress-ng score of 97,945.78. Memory bandwidth reaches 444.43 GB/s for large uncached reads and 188.83 GB/s for writes, reflecting strong scale across wide memory channels. In-memory data store testing yielded 130.32 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads alongside a PassMark database score of 37,422.58. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 609.06 GB/s.

The configuration offers high resource density for workloads requiring vast memory coupled with dedicated high-frequency cores and high-capacity NVMe storage. Because the instance lacks discrete GPU acceleration and includes no default public IPv4 addresses, it is unsuited for GPU-bound training. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, complex relational database management systems, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise simulations.
description: Microsoft Azure FX96mds_v2 is a compute and memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture with 48 physical cores, the instance includes 260 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX matrix acceleration. The platform delivers 1,832 GB of system memory, providing 19.08 GB per vCPU, paired with 5,669 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show exceptional throughput, reaching 444.43 GB/s in large-block uncached memory reads, 130.32 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, and a PassMark CPU score of 103,610.4. While lacking hardware accelerators such as GPUs, the dense memory allocation and high single-core frequency maximize efficiency for memory-constrained workloads without requiring clustered overhead. FX96mds_v2 is engineered for enterprise in-memory databases, large relational database operations, high-throughput caching tiers, and memory-heavy scientific computing simulations.
